questions.question: Which of the following is included among the descriptive studies?
What is the main limitation of a case report?
wrong_answers: A. It is expensive and time-consuming
C. lt requires large sample sizes

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes descriptive studies?
questions.correct_answer: C. They identify patterns of disease and generate hypotheses
wrong_answers: A. They are designed to establish causal relationships
B. They always include a control or comparison group
D. They have limited usefulness for public health planning

questions.question: A physician reported 5 unusual cases of severe jaundice in newborns, history revealed that their mothers were taking Tetracycline during pregnancy. What is the type of epidemiological study design?

In a review of health data, researchers find that communities with higher levels of physical activity report lower rates of obesity. They conclude that all individuals in these communities have a lower risk of being obese due to higher levels of physical activity. What type of bias does this conclusion exhibit?
Which of the following study designs is describing a case of cervical cancer in a 20 years old female?
Which of the following best defines a confounding factor?
questions.correct_answer: B. A variable related to both exposure and outcome and distorts the association
wrong_answers: A. A variable that lies on the causal pathway between exposure and outcome
C. A variable that occurs after the outcome and cannot influence the relationship
D. A variable that is unrelated to both the exposure and the outcome

questions.question: Researchers want to investigate the relationship between smoking status and chronic respiratory disease among adults in a city. They select 1, 000 adults and assess both smoking habits and lung function on the same day. What is the type of this epidemiological study design?
Which type of descriptive study provides a 'snapshot' of the prevalence of a disease or health-related characteristic in a population at a single point in time?
A study that compares disease rates and exposures across different populations or communities, rather than individuals, what is the name of this study?
What is the main feature of the cross-sectional study design?
questions.correct_answer: C. It measures the exposure & outcome simultaneously in a population at a specific point in time.
wrong_answers: A. Subjects are followed over a long period of time.
B. lt compares two groups: subjects with a disease to subjects without the disease.
D. It is the only design that establishes a cause-and-effect relationship

questions.question: A hospital doctor reports a single unusual case of anthrax after exposure to imported animal furs. What is this study design?

An investigator wants to estimate the prevalence of obesity among university students. Beside weight and height measurements, he also distributes an online questionnaire asking about age, gender, and smoking. What is the type of the study design?
Five children with hepatoblastoma (rare form of cancer liver) were reported. History showed past exposure to a specific insecticide. What is the type of this study design?

In 2024, researchers measured body mass index (BMI) and physical activity levels among office employees at the same point in time. They assessed the association between physical inactivity and obesity. Which type of study design best describes this investigation?
A cross-sectional study of a town's population of 10, 000 found that 400 people have hypertension. What is the prevalence of hypertension per 1, 000 population?
questions.correct_answer: B. School context or standard calculation matches 40 per 1, 000

questions.question: A research team wished to investigate a possible association between tobacco use and oral lesions among a group of workers. At periodic employment examination, each worker was asked about tobacco use, and a dentist examined them for the presence of oral lesions. What is the type of the study design?

During pre-placement examination of 200 new employees, 20 persons were hypertensive among 80 smokers, while 6 hypertensive persons were detected among the remaining 120 non-smokers, What is the prevalence of hypertension among smokers in this study?
An investigator collected data on infant mortality rates in different governorates of Egypt and the average family size in these governorates in the year 2005. What is the type of the design?
Which of the following is an advantage of correlation study?
wrong_answers: B. Data are available on the individual level
D. The risk of exposure is calculated

questions.question: What is the epidemiological study design that measures the association between two different quantitative variables?
Which of the following is a key limitation of cross-sectional studies?
Which of the following is an advantage of a cross-sectional study?
questions.correct_answer: B. Can measure prevalence in a population
wrong_answers: A. Can determine temporality between exposure and disease
